claims.text: Conventional laser powder-bed fusion of AlCrFeNiSi without build-plate preheating typically produces compositional segregation.
Conventional laser powder-bed fusion of AlCrFeNiSi without build-plate preheating typically produces high residual stresses.
Conventional laser powder-bed fusion of AlCrFeNiSi without build-plate preheating typically produces a defect-rich microstructure.
The proposed intervention is a build-plate preheat of approximately 300–600 °C during laser powder-bed fusion.
Elevated build-plate preheating reduces thermal gradients during solidification of additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Reduced thermal gradients caused by build-plate preheating slow the cooling rate.
The slower, controlled cooling promotes homogenization of the multi-principal elements in AlCrFeNiSi.
Elevated build-plate preheating reduces elemental segregation in laser powder-bed-fused AlCrFeNiSi.
Elevated build-plate preheating reduces residual thermal stress in laser powder-bed-fused AlCrFeNiSi.
Elevated build-plate preheating limits defect nucleation and lowers defect density in laser powder-bed-fused AlCrFeNiSi.
The preheated AlCrFeNiSi samples will have higher tensile strength than samples fabricated without build-plate preheating.
The preheated AlCrFeNiSi samples will have higher tensile ductility than samples fabricated without build-plate preheating.
Reductions in segregation, residual stress, and defects will improve the mechanical integrity of AlCrFeNiSi.
The intervention is applicable to AlCrFeNiSi laser powder-bed fusion under an inert argon atmosphere.
A suitable preheat range can avoid oxidation and other thermal degradation of AlCrFeNiSi powder or builds.
High-temperature processing presents a potential oxidation risk for an alloy containing Al, Cr, and Si.
High-temperature preheating may alter powder behavior.
The effect may not extend to other alloy systems or manufacturing methods.
